lead: Slice 1 of the GitLab Pages port is built: the app now also runs entirely in Chrome, with nothing installed and nothing uploaded. It reads the part and shows the 3D model the same as the Python app; it runs no checks yet, and every step says so. You approved the merge once the checks passed; they passed, so it is going in now.
try: View-only demo: 19 test parts, each analyzed in advance by the new browser engine. Tap a part, then walk the five steps.

After the merge, turn on the public test copy once: on github.com open the repository, tap Settings, then Pages, and set Source to GitHub Actions. The next push to main publishes it; I'll send the link.
measured: The browser engine gives the Python app's answer on 77 of 77 quick-set files (part size, faces, every mesh point, assumptions, refusals).
Tests: 926 service, 37 web, 78 service-page and 24 browser-copy tests pass. 65 older page tests wait for the slices that port their features (listed, slice by slice).
Page stays usable while a part is analyzed: the longest pause 20 to 26 ms, taps answered in 22 to 35 ms (limit 200 ms, 4 runs).
Drawing the finished part: 310 to 484 ms in the test browser (software graphics). The Python app freezes 1,144 to 1,387 ms on the same file.

Big test plate (49.94 MB, 12,544 holes): not finished in the 60-minute limit in the browser (the tab was at 3.3 GB after 53 minutes); Python's own reader alone takes 15.4 minutes on it. The 6.1 MB NIST FTC 09 file before it read fine. Next step: pick a plate size that finishes (your D-058 call, at S2).

Full set, before merging: 290 files: 282 the same; 6 crash the Python app (old UMD files) and open in the browser copy; 2 differ only in the 3D mesh, on 3 faces (points up to 0.35 mm apart, from the two OpenCascade versions). The mesh only draws the part in this slice; S4 checks it before pockets and walls use it.
decisions: Page freeze: found and fixed. The engine now loads while the page waits for a file, the 3D view's lines are worked out in the background, and all edges draw as one. The 200 ms limit stays, measured during the analysis.
Big test plate: runs once per slice, alone, with a 60-minute limit, not on every push.
later: No checks yet: holes come in S2, then plan, cost and the PDF in S3 (the first version engineers at work can use).
The Inventor .ipt field is hidden until S7.
A crash inside the engine shows the usual "The analysis failed" message, but no test can make the engine crash on purpose yet.
plan: Done: trial, spec, S1 site, viewer and parity check.
Next: S2 holes, S3 plan, cost and PDF, S4 pockets, S5 walls, S6 turning, S7 Inventor, S8 retire Python.
